recommendation: Keep the audit commit as-is. No follow-up source work is needed for FHIR-29804 unless a work group requests a new substantive revision to the Medication Definition Module.
issue_request: FHIR-29804 was a Published/Persuasive R4 change request for R5 from BR&R. It requested applying the attached subgroup wording changes to the Medication Definition Module page, approved Peter Bomberg / Marti Velezis 4-0-0 on 2020-11-30.
initial_application: Commit 05593c5ca5dbfc6b60ca1ef50d4088be30695c2f explicitly applied the issue with subject "Medication definition module wording changes FHIR#29804". The patch updated source/medication-definition-module.html to include co-packaged devices and possible ingredient substances, change the product-definition language from "have" to "can specify", and clean up the PackagedProductDefinition, ManufacturedItemDefinition, and example wording.
additional_context: The Medication Definition module remains in the current build: source/modules-list.html links medication-definition-module.html, and source/fhir.ini lists the Medication Definition resources as active resources. Later edits renamed ClinicalUseIssue to ClinicalUseDefinition and FHIR-31736 added Relationship to Prescribing guidance; those adjacent changes preserve rather than reverse the FHIR-29804 wording. The Jira attachment URL returned 403 during reconciliation, but the Jira snapshot identifies the attachment and the same-day FHIR#29804 source commit supplies the implementation evidence.
reconciliation: No source edit was made. The latest combined branch still contains the applied FHIR-29804 wording in source/medication-definition-module.html, so an empty audit commit was published.
